purpose: Which named stops of this lane are LEGITIMATE STOPS and which are OUTAGES, and
how often each is allowed to page the owner. This file is the taxonomy; the
behaviour is in scripts/journalist_query_scan.py and is asserted by
The distinction this lane is built on is stated in its own workflow: 'a day
with no relevant queries is a PASS and sends nothing. A failure means the lane
could not look, or looked and could not read what it found.' Those are the two
classes below. Everything the lane can stop for is one or the other, and the
class decides both the exit code and the noise.

legitimate_stop: The lane worked and there was nothing to do, or it is waiting on something
that has never been set up. GREEN. Announced once so the owner knows it is
waiting, then silent -- a daily issue reading 'still not subscribed' is a
standing instruction nobody follows, and this repository has already paid
outage: Something that WAS working has stopped, and the lane is no longer reading
her mail. RED, and it stays red every run until it is fixed: an outage that
goes green on its own is a false green over a lane that is not doing its
job. What is deduplicated is the ISSUE, not the failure. The run is red
every time; the owner is paged once and then reminded on the cadence below,
instead of receiving a fresh issue twice a weekday forever.

reminder_days_meaning: Days between repeat announcements while the stop is unresolved. The stop is
announced immediately the first time. 0 means announce once and never again.
An outage is reminded because it is fixable and someone must act; a
legitimate stop is not, because nothing is wrong.

why: The three IMAP secrets are not set at all. The lane was built before the
owner subscribed to Source of Sources, so 'not configured yet' is a
designed state and not a break. It is announced once and then waits.
The secrets ARE set and the mailbox refused them. This is categorically
different from NO_MAILBOX_CREDENTIAL: something that was reading her mail
has stopped, and every SOS digest that arrives while it is broken is a
citation opportunity that expires unread. Deadlines in these digests are
measured in hours.
First seen 2026-09-09 12:25 UTC. The lane had been green on every run
through 2026-09-08 18:30 UTC. The credential is a Google app password and
the owner changed her Google account password that morning, which revokes
app passwords and Gmail-scoped OAuth refresh tokens alike. That is a
rotation only she can perform; there is no code change here that restores
authentication, and anything that made this look green would be a false
green over a lane that is genuinely not reading her mail.
Reminded weekly rather than twice a weekday: 10 issues a week is the
shape of notification that gets muted, and a muted outage is a silent one.
The IMAP host could not be reached or the TLS session failed. Usually
transient, but indistinguishable from a permanent break without acting on
it, and a lane that cannot look is red for the same reason as one that
cannot read.
--inbox-dir was pointed at something that is not a directory. Local
operator error; it never occurs on the scheduled run, so it is never
announced, but it must not be mistaken for a quiet day.
No drafting model key. Queries are still read, surfaced and recorded --
the digest just arrives without drafts. Degraded, not blind.
A message arrived that is not a query digest, most often the SOS welcome
email. Recorded so it is never counted as a digest, which is the small
dishonesty that would make 'nothing relevant today' believable when it
was not true.
Some queries in a digest did not match the format grammar. The rest were
read. Reported rather than hidden, because a grammar that silently drops
half a digest looks exactly like a thin news day.
The model declined or failed for one query. The query is still surfaced;
she can answer it without a draft.
Real queries were found and the issue that hands them to her could not be
opened. The whole lane exists to deliver that one notification, so
failing to deliver it is a failure of the lane. Not announced, because
the announcement path is the thing that just failed -- it fails the run
loudly instead.
The issue explaining another stop could not be opened, so the stop was
NOT marked announced and the next run tries again. Red, because a
notification lane that fails silently is indistinguishable from one that
had nothing to say.
The scan raised something no named stop covers. It exists so that a crash
can never again leave yesterday's receipt in place: on 2026-09-09 an
unhandled imaplib traceback skipped the receipt write, and the workflow's
own reporting step then read the PREVIOUS run's file and announced 'NO
RELEVANT QUERIES: 10 queries were read from 1 digest(s)' on a morning the
lane had read nothing at all. A stale receipt is the precise failure this
lane was built to prevent -- a quiet day and a broken lane looking the
same -- reintroduced in the error path.
